definitions.explanation: The horizontal piece at the bottom of a doorway or sliding door frame in Japanese architecture.
Used figuratively to describe psychological barriers or difficulty in approaching something.

examples.japanese: {敷居|しきい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{踏|ふ}まない→踏む：01197_fumu⟧⟦ように→ように：10081_youni⟧⟦{注意|ちゅうい}して→注意する：01464_chuui⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please be careful not to step on the threshold.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{敷居|しきい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦すり{減|へ}っている→すり減る：10381_suriheru⟧。
examples.english: The thresholds in old houses are worn down.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦レストラン→レストラン：01048_resutoran⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{敷居|しきい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧。
examples.english: This restaurant feels intimidating (hard to enter).

examples.japanese: {敷居|しきい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}くて→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦{入|はい}り→入る：00494_hairu⟧⟦にくい→にくい：02005_nikui⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: It's a shop that's hard to go into (feels exclusive).

examples.japanese: ⟦{和室|わしつ}→和室：10437_washitsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{敷居|しきい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦ぶつけた→ぶつける：02413_butsukeru⟧。
examples.english: I hit my foot on the Japanese-style room's threshold.

examples.japanese: ⟦{引|ひ}き{戸|ど}→引き戸：27509_hikido⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{敷居|しきい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{溝|みぞ}→溝：09410_mizo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ゴミ→ゴミ：00840_gomi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{溜|た}まっている→溜まる：02067_tamaru⟧。
examples.english: Dust has accumulated in the groove of the sliding door's threshold.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{敷居|しきい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{座|すわ}って→座る：00757_suwaru⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いけない→いけない：02335_ikenai⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{教|おそ}わった→教わる：02024_osowaru⟧。
examples.english: I was taught that children shouldn't sit on the threshold.

examples.japanese: ⟦{初心者|しょしんしゃ}→初心者：10149_shoshinsha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{敷居|しきい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦かもしれない→かもしれない：00164_kamoshirenai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{慣|な}れれば→慣れる：00870_nareru⟧⟦{楽|たの}しい→楽しい：00817_tanoshii⟧。
examples.english: It might feel intimidating for beginners, but once you get used to it, it's fun.

examples.japanese: {敷居|しきい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{低|ひく}くして→低い：02947_hikui⟧、⟦{誰|だれ}→誰：00534_dare⟧⟦でも→でも：noentry⟧⟦{参加|さんか}できる→参加する：02498_sanka⟧⟦ように→ように：10081_youni⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: We lowered the barrier so that anyone could participate.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{高級|こうきゅう}→高級：08644_koukyuu⟧⟦ホテル→ホテル：01027_hoteru⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{敷居|しきい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}くて→高い：00500_takai⟧、⟦なかなか→なかなか：01547_nakanaka⟧⟦{行|い}けない→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: That luxury hotel feels so exclusive that I can never bring myself to go.

notes:
JAPANESE ARCHITECTURE: In traditional rooms with sliding doors (⟦{襖|ふすま}→襖：03908_fusuma⟧ or ⟦{障子|しょうじ}→障子：04201_shouji⟧), the {敷居|しきい} is the grooved bottom track the doors slide along. The matching upper track is the ⟦{鴨居|かもい}→鴨居：08107_kamoi⟧.

CULTURAL NOTE: {敷居|しきい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{踏|ふ}む→踏む：01197_fumu⟧ (stepping on the threshold) is traditionally bad manners - the sill was seen as standing for the household itself, so guests step over it rather than on it. Stepping on it also wears down the groove and makes the doors stick.

KEY IDIOM: {敷居|しきい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧
- Literally: "the threshold is high"
- Meaning: a place or activity feels intimidating or hard to approach
- Used of establishments that feel exclusive or expensive, and of hobbies and fields that seem to demand expertise
- Opposite: {敷居|しきい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{低|ひく}くする→低い：02947_hikui⟧, to make something easier for newcomers to approach

NOTE ON USAGE: Traditionally the idiom meant feeling too awkward to revisit somewhere after some failing or breach on one's own part. The modern sense - "too upmarket or too advanced for me" - is now the dominant one and is what learners will hear, though prescriptive style guides still object to it.

RELATED ARCHITECTURE:
- ⟦{鴨居|かもい}→鴨居：08107_kamoi⟧ - lintel, the upper track
- ⟦{襖|ふすま}→襖：03908_fusuma⟧ - opaque sliding doors
- ⟦{障子|しょうじ}→障子：04201_shouji⟧ - translucent paper screens
- ⟦{和室|わしつ}→和室：10437_washitsu⟧ - Japanese-style room
